Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@clearwell.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options and throughput for Q4 ramp

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're closing our Q4 vendor shortlist and need a clear recommendation on how to package Redwood for our platform team. A few constraints to share up front:

- Expected token throughput: ~1.2B tokens/month starting Nov, spiking to ~3B in Feb.
- Low-latency inference for synchronous chat endpoints (95th pctl < 350ms) but fine to route batch/async to cheaper variants.
- Data residency: our EU testbed will ramp in Jan (may require Dedicated or VPC options then).

Specific asks:
1) Can you recommend a clean upgrade path vs starting on a high-throughput plan? We want predictable pricing as we scale and a path that avoids lengthy procurement each quarter.
2) How do feature bundles (streaming, function calls, structured output) map to plan tiers and add-ons? We need to understand what's included vs add-on pricing.
3) Any room for tier-consolidation discount if we commit to a 12-month usage floor across hosted + dedicated burst?

Attached is a one-week sample of usage metrics and a rough list of endpoints (clearwell_current_usage.csv).

Would love a short decision matrix (2–3 scenarios) with pros/cons and an ask to your pricing/sales lead if we want a committed discount.

Best,
Sasha
Sasha Patel
Head of Platform
Clearwell Labs

Attachments: clearwell_current_usage.csv (CSV, 45KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha@clearwell.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options and throughput for Q4 ramp

Hi Sasha —

Thanks — got the sample. I pulled a quick first-cut matrix and attached scenario workup (tier_scenarios_v1.xlsx) and a short pricing summary (pricing_summary_v2.pdf). High level:

Scenario A — Gradual hosted-to-dedicated ramp (low commitment)
- Start on Hosted Standard + Add-on: streaming + structured outputs.
- Autoscale to Dedicated reserved pools when 95th pctl or cost targets hit.
- Pros: fast onboarding, no procurement. Cons: unit cost higher during sustained peak.

Scenario B — 12-month hybrid commit (recommended for predictability)
- Commit to a 12-month reserved capacity baseline (Dedicated small pool) + hosted overflow.
- Include feature bundle (streaming + function calls + eval monitoring) in tier; bandwidth pricing tiers reduce at 1.5B/month.
- Pros: predictable unit economics, preferred routing and capacity SLAs. Cons: procurement lead time.

Scenario C — Dedicated-first (throughput-critical)
- Full Dedicated deployment with on-prem/private option for EU testbed.
- Pros: lowest variable cost at scale, isolation for compliance. Cons: longer setup and higher upfront.

Pricing/discounts: We can offer a commit discount tied to baseline capacity and a step-down clause for gradual overage handling. Ben (cc'd) is managing commercial concessions; Lauren handles large-deal approvals and can advise on acceptable structures.

Quick clarifying Qs before we finalize a recommended matrix:
- Is the EU testbed soft requirement or a hard compliance requirement for production?
- Do you expect steady month-over-month growth (linear) or a one-time spike followed by steady state?

If you're available, we can run a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the matrix and pick a preferred scenario to price.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: tier_scenarios_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB), pricing_summary_v2.pdf (PDF, 60KB)

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the matrix — that's close to what we need. Quick answers:
- EU testbed is a hard requirement for any customer-facing work in Q1 (data residency compliance).
- Growth looks like a steady ramp: Nov = 1.2B, Dec = 1.6B, Jan = 2.2B, Feb = 3B (forecast).

Two follow-ups before we lock:
1) For Scenario B, can you show the blended $/1M tokens at 1.2B vs 3B with the proposed commit discount? We need to justify to finance.
2) Will the Reserved baseline require an annual up-front payment or monthly invoicing with minimums?

Also, would Redwood be open to a short-term pilot discount for the first two months (we're sensitive to Q4 budget windows)?

Happy to do a call tomorrow 10–10:30 PT.

—Sasha
